A hallmark is three small stamps, and in most of the world only one of them is required by law.

The fineness mark states purity in parts per thousand — 750 for 18-karat gold, 925 for sterling silver. Where hallmarking is compulsory, like the UK, an assay office mark means an independent lab tested the metal. In the US, there's no such requirement — the karat stamp is the seller's own claim, checked only after the fact if it's wrong.
